- Diversified business portfolio across EPC, FMS and MSW, which management says helps mitigate risk in one business type through another
- Experience of working with large and renowned clients on challenging projects

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Working capital risk in the EPC business — The Company states its major EPC SBU requires immediate and continuous fund allocation during project execution, and that delays in securing working capital risk project delays or stalemate and can impair project viability through delay or escalation in the cost of capital. Mitigation cited is gradually decreasing the share of EPC projects in the overall portfolio while diversifying project streams, and engaging leading financial institutions for funding facilities and credit lines. The SWOT also lists high working capital and labour intensity of the businesses as a weakness.
- Customer concentration risk — Concentration in any one business or geography exposes the Company to financial setbacks if one or a few large customers move away or delay cash flows; the Company notes knock-on risk to other clients and projects from financial blockades and to management bandwidth spent reviving erring clients or projects. Mitigation is geographic, industry-wise and service-offering-wise diversification plus a shift in mix between private and government clients.
- Over-reliance on B2G (business-to-government) revenue — Listed explicitly as a weakness in the Company's own SWOT analysis. It sits alongside the stated threat that repeated failures in nursing State Electricity Boards back to financial health may stop investment in power generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure — i.e. the counterparty is largely the public sector.
- Execution risk in complex operating environments — The Company cites availability of suitable manpower, raw material procurement, legal and commercial documentation, project-level investments, and challenging topography and extreme weather; any deficiency can delay execution, causing cost escalation and penalties. Mitigation cited: professional liability insurance, stringent SOPs and project manuals, multiple sourcing for raw materials, periodic project monitoring, and sharing execution risk through partnerships from time to time.
- Legal and contractual risk — Given the scale, complexity and duration of projects, the Company says contractual disputes, claims and litigation may arise and potentially impact project outcomes and financial performance. Mitigation is a structured contract review and approval process with dedicated legal and commercial teams, and incorporating learnings from past disputes.
- Talent / human capital risk — The Company describes its business as human capital intensive, requiring it to attract and retain talented and skilled manpower; failure to hire or retain talent is stated to be likely to impact business operations (the disclosure is truncated in this extract before the mitigation is fully set out).
- Macro-economic and interest-rate / policy risk — The Company says its business depends on the country's economic developments and market demand, that macro developments affect its cost of capital through central bank policy rates, and that government spending and policy responses can affect the industry and the Company. Mitigation is diversifying revenue streams and SBUs, geographic diversification of project presence within India, and working on reducing the cost of capital and debt through repayment and one-time settlements with banks and financial institutions.
- Competitive intensity and sector-specific demand threats — The Company's own threat list names competition gaining inroads in its segments on the back of increased demand, availability of funds and advent of technology, and the risk that stressed telecom balance sheets constrain upgrades of existing infrastructure — both bearing directly on EPC and telecom order flow.

business.body: The Company, along with its subsidiaries and associates, executes EPC work in power transmission & distribution and telecom infrastructure, provides integrated facility management services, and works with urban local bodies on municipal solid waste collection, transportation, segregation, processing, treatment and disposal, largely in north India and aligned with the Swachh Bharat mission. Its FMS offering integrates multiple services under one roof for facilities such as corporate offices, malls, railway stations, railway coaches, airports, ports, commercial establishments, monuments, parks and beaches. Patrons include global MNCs, Indian companies, PSUs and the Government sector.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no specific capex project with a commissioning, completion or ramp timeline. Expansion is stated only as intent and footprint. In Engineering Services the Company says it continues to selectively pursue profitable, feasible and sustainable projects while evaluating opportunities in 5G telecom infrastructure, water and sewage distribution networks, gas distribution networks, Smart Cities / Metro-linked infrastructure, and Fixed Asset Management / O&M services; the Group says it will focus on technology-enabled execution, complex infrastructure projects and selective expansion into emerging opportunities such as renewable and associated power infrastructure, and remains committed to strengthening its EPC order pipeline and execution capabilities. In MSW, the Group says that going forward it will focus on technology-driven MSW projects, advanced waste processing, resource recovery and waste-to-energy solutions — stated as a forward focus, not as commissioned capacity. In FMS the Company says it is strategically focused on expanding the FMS business over the upcoming financial years and, on the technology side, has launched the FMEdge App, a digital platform for employee attendance management and employee-related services. On footprint, the Group reports a presence in India and selected overseas markets including Nepal, Uganda and Tanzania, and says it has completed projects in Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, Odisha, Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh. No new plant, site, capacity addition, debottlenecking or commissioning date is disclosed in this text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Group sees strong long-term opportunities in its EPC business, supported by India's expanding power infrastructure, grid modernisation, electrification and telecom network requirements
- Indian EPC industry expected to maintain a healthy growth trajectory on continued government infrastructure spending, rising private-sector capex, industrial expansion and investment across transportation, energy and utilities
- CRISIL cited: large, diversified EPC companies expected to see 9-11% revenue growth, supported by infrastructure capital expenditure, healthy order books and faster project execution
- India's power T&D EPC market growth supported by planned integration of over 500 GW of renewable capacity by 2030 and over 600 GW by 2032, ISTS/InSTS expansion, grid modernisation, advanced transmission technologies and HVDC deployment
- National Electricity Plan cited: approximately Rs 9.15 lakh crore expected to be invested in transmission infrastructure by 2032
- Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) has opened the transmission sector to broader participation, promoting competition and transparent procurement
- The Indian power T&D EPC market is entering a 'Triple Transition' — simultaneous shifts in power generation, consumption patterns and grid infrastructure — requiring extensive transmission and distribution upgrades and creating new opportunities for EPC contractors
- India's connectivity evolution expected to sustain demand for telecom infrastructure across 5G deployment, fibre backhaul, network densification, transmission infrastructure, data centres and associated power and passive infrastructure
- For EPC and infrastructure service providers, the telecom evolution presents opportunities across engineering, procurement, project execution, fibre deployment, network infrastructure and associated electrical and civil works
- Standalone revenue growth of 134.68% in FY2025-26 attributed primarily to growth in standalone operations, particularly completion of work and final billing in various projects; the Company nevertheless continued to report a loss at the standalone level
- Macro backdrop cited: India growth projected at 6.4 percent by the IMF, India's real GDP up 7.7% in FY2025-26 per MoSPI, with domestic demand and sustained investment momentum as anchors; global headline inflation rising to 4.7 percent in 2026 and crude oil prices projected up 32 percent in 2026 versus 2025
- The Group remains committed to strengthening its EPC order pipeline and execution capabilities to deliver sustainable growth in the coming years (no order-book value disclosed in this text)
- Industry context only: CRISIL notes large, diversified EPC companies are supported by healthy order books; government-led infrastructure investment supports project opportunities and order inflows

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Facility Management Services (FMS):** Integrated Facility Management Services, Mechanized & High-Pressure Cleaning Services, Manpower Supply & Workforce Management, Building Operations & Maintenance (BOM), Electrical & Utility Maintenance Services, Comprehensive Annual Maintenance Contracts, Pest Control & Hygiene Management, Pantry, Hospitality & Support Services, Railway & Transit Facility Support Services, Facility Helpdesk & Service Management, Energy & Resource Management, FMEdge App
- **Municipal Solid Waste Management (MSW):** Collection & Transportation (C&T) of municipal solid waste, Segregation and processing of municipal solid waste, Treatment and disposal of solid waste
- **Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC):** Power Transmission & Distribution (T&D) EPC, Telecom infrastructure EPC

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Government and urban local bodies (B2G) — the Company notes over-reliance on B2G business
- PSUs and Government sector clients
- Indian companies and global MNCs
- Corporate offices, malls and commercial establishments
- Railway stations and railway coaches; airports and ports
- Monuments, parks and beaches
- North India (MSW collection & transportation largely in north India)
- Projects executed across multiple geographies within India

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Group sees strong long-term opportunities in its EPC business, supported by India's expanding power infrastructure, grid modernisation, electrification and telecom network requirements
- Indian EPC industry expected to maintain a healthy growth trajectory on continued government infrastructure spending, rising private-sector capex, industrial expansion and investment across transportation, energy and utilities
- CRISIL cited: large, diversified EPC companies expected to see 9-11% revenue growth, supported by infrastructure capital expenditure, healthy order books and faster project execution
- India's power T&D EPC market growth supported by planned integration of over 500 GW of renewable capacity by 2030 and over 600 GW by 2032, ISTS/InSTS expansion, grid modernisation, advanced transmission technologies and HVDC deployment
- National Electricity Plan cited: approximately Rs 9.15 lakh crore expected to be invested in transmission infrastructure by 2032
- Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) has opened the transmission sector to broader participation, promoting competition and transparent procurement
- The Indian power T&D EPC market is entering a 'Triple Transition' — simultaneous shifts in power generation, consumption patterns and grid infrastructure — requiring extensive transmission and distribution upgrades and creating new opportunities for EPC contractors
- India's connectivity evolution expected to sustain demand for telecom infrastructure across 5G deployment, fibre backhaul, network densification, transmission infrastructure, data centres and associated power and passive infrastructure
- For EPC and infrastructure service providers, the telecom evolution presents opportunities across engineering, procurement, project execution, fibre deployment, network infrastructure and associated electrical and civil works
- Standalone revenue growth of 134.68% in FY2025-26 attributed primarily to growth in standalone operations, particularly completion of work and final billing in various projects; the Company nevertheless continued to report a loss at the standalone level
- Macro backdrop cited: India growth projected at 6.4 percent by the IMF, India's real GDP up 7.7% in FY2025-26 per MoSPI, with domestic demand and sustained investment momentum as anchors; global headline inflation rising to 4.7 percent in 2026 and crude oil prices projected up 32 percent in 2026 versus 2025
- The Group remains committed to strengthening its EPC order pipeline and execution capabilities to deliver sustainable growth in the coming years (no order-book value disclosed in this text)
- Industry context only: CRISIL notes large, diversified EPC companies are supported by healthy order books; government-led infrastructure investment supports project opportunities and order inflows

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Build on established expertise in Power T&D and Telecom EPC with a focus on technology-enabled execution and complex infrastructure projects
- Selective expansion into emerging opportunities such as renewable and associated power infrastructure
- Strengthen the EPC order pipeline and execution capabilities to deliver sustainable growth in the coming years
- Operate through three Strategic Business Units — EPC (Power T&D and Telecom infrastructure), Facility Management Services and Municipal Solid Waste Management

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report describes no specific capex project with a commissioning, completion or ramp timeline. Expansion is stated only as intent and footprint. In Engineering Services the Company says it continues to selectively pursue profitable, feasible and sustainable projects while evaluating opportunities in 5G telecom infrastructure, water and sewage distribution networks, gas distribution networks, Smart Cities / Metro-linked infrastructure, and Fixed Asset Management / O&M services; the Group says it will focus on technology-enabled execution, complex infrastructure projects and selective expansion into emerging opportunities such as renewable and associated power infrastructure, and remains committed to strengthening its EPC order pipeline and execution capabilities. In MSW, the Group says that going forward it will focus on technology-driven MSW projects, advanced waste processing, resource recovery and waste-to-energy solutions — stated as a forward focus, not as commissioned capacity. In FMS the Company says it is strategically focused on expanding the FMS business over the upcoming financial years and, on the technology side, has launched the FMEdge App, a digital platform for employee attendance management and employee-related services. On footprint, the Group reports a presence in India and selected overseas markets including Nepal, Uganda and Tanzania, and says it has completed projects in Jammu & Kashmir, Rajasthan, Odisha, Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Kerala, Chhattisgarh, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh. No new plant, site, capacity addition, debottlenecking or commissioning date is disclosed in this text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified business portfolio across EPC, FMS and MSW, which management says helps mitigate risk in one business type through another
- Experience of working with large and renowned clients on challenging projects
- Differentiated organizational capabilities across business segments through technology and processes
- Compliance and Corporate Governance
- Illustrious track record created over 20+ years
- Fungibility of resources across segments
- Sizeable trained and skilled workforce
- Innovation capabilities
- Reduced debt of the company
- Integration of multiple facility management services under one roof, positioning the Company strongly in the growing Integrated Facility Management Services market
- MSW mandates won not only on competitive pricing but on the technology used in collection, treatment and disposal through scientific methods

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Working capital risk in the EPC business — The Company states its major EPC SBU requires immediate and continuous fund allocation during project execution, and that delays in securing working capital risk project delays or stalemate and can impair project viability through delay or escalation in the cost of capital. Mitigation cited is gradually decreasing the share of EPC projects in the overall portfolio while diversifying project streams, and engaging leading financial institutions for funding facilities and credit lines. The SWOT also lists high working capital and labour intensity of the businesses as a weakness.
- Customer concentration risk — Concentration in any one business or geography exposes the Company to financial setbacks if one or a few large customers move away or delay cash flows; the Company notes knock-on risk to other clients and projects from financial blockades and to management bandwidth spent reviving erring clients or projects. Mitigation is geographic, industry-wise and service-offering-wise diversification plus a shift in mix between private and government clients.
- Over-reliance on B2G (business-to-government) revenue — Listed explicitly as a weakness in the Company's own SWOT analysis. It sits alongside the stated threat that repeated failures in nursing State Electricity Boards back to financial health may stop investment in power generation, transmission and distribution infrastructure — i.e. the counterparty is largely the public sector.
- Execution risk in complex operating environments — The Company cites availability of suitable manpower, raw material procurement, legal and commercial documentation, project-level investments, and challenging topography and extreme weather; any deficiency can delay execution, causing cost escalation and penalties. Mitigation cited: professional liability insurance, stringent SOPs and project manuals, multiple sourcing for raw materials, periodic project monitoring, and sharing execution risk through partnerships from time to time.
- Legal and contractual risk — Given the scale, complexity and duration of projects, the Company says contractual disputes, claims and litigation may arise and potentially impact project outcomes and financial performance. Mitigation is a structured contract review and approval process with dedicated legal and commercial teams, and incorporating learnings from past disputes.
- Talent / human capital risk — The Company describes its business as human capital intensive, requiring it to attract and retain talented and skilled manpower; failure to hire or retain talent is stated to be likely to impact business operations (the disclosure is truncated in this extract before the mitigation is fully set out).
- Macro-economic and interest-rate / policy risk — The Company says its business depends on the country's economic developments and market demand, that macro developments affect its cost of capital through central bank policy rates, and that government spending and policy responses can affect the industry and the Company. Mitigation is diversifying revenue streams and SBUs, geographic diversification of project presence within India, and working on reducing the cost of capital and debt through repayment and one-time settlements with banks and financial institutions.
- Competitive intensity and sector-specific demand threats — The Company's own threat list names competition gaining inroads in its segments on the back of increased demand, availability of funds and advent of technology, and the risk that stressed telecom balance sheets constrain upgrades of existing infrastructure — both bearing directly on EPC and telecom order flow.
